abstract: Audits onboard trauma equipment availability and resuscitation bay turnaround timing
system_message:
You are the Maritime medical director (MED). Your business responsibilities include auditing onboard trauma equipment availability and resuscitation bay turnaround timing, as well as reviewing medical gas storage for offshore rescue vessels.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Audits onboard trauma equipment availability and resuscitation bay turnaround timing（CLINIC）
information_points.content:
MED-CLINIC-T1X：Records for the Southern Cross Emergency Responder confirm an operable trauma stabilization unit onboard, with an intensive care bed preparation duration of 18 min required to ready a critical care bay.
MED-CLINIC-ONU：For the Pacific Guardian Fast Rescue Cutter, verification confirms the presence of an operable high-acuity trauma stabilization unit onboard, and clinical emergency drill records demonstrate an intensive care bed preparation duration of 18 min to sterilize and configure a critical care bay.
MED-CLINIC-GTT：The Nordic Sentinel Multipurpose Vessel maintains an operable high-acuity trauma stabilization unit onboard, while its intensive care bed preparation duration was recorded at 24 min during critical care bay readiness drills.

information_points.title: Medical gas storage（OXYGEN）
information_points.content:
MED-OXYGEN-A3S：According to the gas cylinder manifold certificate for the Pacific Guardian Fast Rescue Cutter, the reserve medical oxygen supply provides an endurance of 40 h supporting four simultaneous high-flow oxygen patients.
MED-OXYGEN-2T1：For the Southern Cross Emergency Responder, standard medical gas reserves document a reserve medical oxygen supply endurance of 80 h for four simultaneous high-flow oxygen patients.
MED-OXYGEN-OM5：The Nordic Sentinel Multipurpose Vessel holds a reserve medical oxygen supply rated for 60 h of continuous endurance for four simultaneous high-flow oxygen patients.
